channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Browns WR Denzel Boston is listed as a starter on Cleveland’s preseason unofficial depth chart.
item.description: Boston, who ESPN’s Benjamin Solak compared to Sam LaPorta after viewing Browns training camp, looks to have a locked in role with the Browns early. We wouldn’t necessarily say that Boston is a lock to be fantasy-useful, but Todd Monken has been well-regarded as an offensive mind and Jerry Jeudy didn’t exactly light it up last year. It’s certainly in the range of outcomes that Boston puts up a WR3/WR4 type of year as a rookie.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson are listed as co-starters on Cleveland’s initial unofficial depth chart.
item.description: They’ve been rotating days for the most part this summer, so this isn’t a surprise. The Browns haven’t named a starter yet, but even when they do, it will be hard to find fantasy value at quarterback.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Free agent CB Terrion Arnold will visit the Giants on Wednesday.
item.description: He’s visited the Saints, Seahawks, and Texans over the past few weeks. It seems likely that Arnold will eventually sign, though perhaps he’ll be in limbo while teams wait for his felony kidnapping and armed robbery charges play out in the courtroom.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort said the Cardinals have no interest in trading Josh Sweat.
item.description: Sweat has been on the PUP list for the entirety of training camp and has not worked out with the team in any way, shape, or form this offseason. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said: “Yeah. I mean, there’s different parts of injuries and stuff like that that, you know, are...and I shouldn’t even call it injuries...but just getting himself right to be ready to roll. So, again, I like where he’s at. I know everyone probably is not believing me on that one, but again, I only try to speak truth to you guys.” Uh huh. Well anyway, we have no idea if Josh Sweat will play again any time soon. It certainly would appear from the outside that Sweat is pushing his leverage towards a trade despite the Cardinals’ denials.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Mercury News’ Cam Inman reports Nick Bosa (knee) is dealing with tendinitis and is “week-to-week.”
item.description: “Pretty normal thing with ACLs,” said Kyle Shanahan. We’re not concerned about Bosa’s status for Week 1 yet, but we’d like to see him practicing.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Chargers T Rashawn Slater said he had a “little flare up” with his knee last week.
item.description: Slater has not practiced since Thursday, but said it is “nothing to be concerned about.” OK, if you say so. After watching how the Christian Darrisaw situation unfolded last year in Minnesota, we think you’re well within your rights to be a little concerned about this even if we’re not in the realm of outright panic just yet.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Puka Nacua left practice early with the trainer on Tuesday and Rams coach Sean McVay said he “isn’t sure what the deal is just yet.”
item.description: Same. We’ll monitor this, but there’s not any actionable advice to hand out until we get a more detailed report. A non-minor Nacua injury, of course, would be stratospheric news in the fantasy community.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Coby Bryant (knee) underwent surgery and will miss 4-6 months.
item.description: “Bears are hoping he can return for the playoffs,” Schefter notes. It’s a brutal blow for the Bears to lose their star free-agent acquisition before training camp even concludes. Chicago didn’t exactly have a stellar defense last year, so perhaps this will make every Bears game a track meet.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Mike Evans (quad) returned to practice on Monday.
item.description: He was limited to individual work, but it’s a good sign that Evans is back on the field at all. It does seem like his quad injury isn’t much to worry about and that he can be drafted with that in mind.-Rivers McCown

item.title: ESPN’s Benjamin Solak reports Deshaun Watson is doing “a lot of short-yardage option running” when he watched training camp.
item.description: Solak believes he is “not sure he’s the same athlete he was before,” but running quarterback is a way that Watson could find some fantasy usefulness in deeper leagues while he’s starting. We’ll believe it when we see it and there’s not a locked in job here for Watson, but perhaps this is a way to make him a bye week starter in superflex leagues.-Rivers McCown
